title: Laptop for Civil Engineering Students (2026): Specs for AutoCAD, Revit, STAAD.Pro and ETABS
summary: Revit and ETABS need 16 GB RAM; AutoCAD and Civil 3D recommend 32 GB. Official requirements of 8 civil tools, Mac options, free student licences, 3 spec tiers.
body_markdown:
## Do you need a graphics card for civil engineering?


**Yes, a discrete one, ideally NVIDIA.** Revit wants a card with at least 4 GB of video memory and recommends 6 to 8 GB. ETABS's DirectX graphics mode asks for a discrete NVIDIA card with 4 GB. Trimble's Tekla recommendations name the GeForce RTX 4060/4070 class and are based on NVIDIA testing.


Integrated graphics will open AutoCAD for 2D drafting. They fall short of Revit's 4 GB guidance once a model has a few floors, and 3D views of a large ETABS model get sluggish. A mid-range NVIDIA GeForce RTX laptop GPU with **8 GB of video memory** covers every tool on this list.

You do **not** need a workstation card (NVIDIA RTX professional) as a student. None of the civil tools above require one.


## Can you use a MacBook for civil engineering?


**Only partly.** AutoCAD has a native Mac version and QGIS runs on macOS. Revit, Civil 3D, STAAD.Pro, ETABS, SAP2000 and Tekla Structures have no Mac version; their makers list Windows only (Tekla 2026: Windows 11 only).


Autodesk does publish a "Parallels Desktop for Mac" configuration for Revit 2026. It asks for 16 GB RAM and 4 GB of video memory dedicated to the Windows virtual machine, and 100 GB of free disk. It also says hardware acceleration is "not recommended" in Parallels. Expect Revit on a Mac to work for small models and to struggle on big ones.


For ETABS, SAP2000, STAAD.Pro and Tekla there is no official Mac route at all. If you already own a Mac, use your college lab for these. If you are buying new for a civil degree, buy Windows.


## Which civil engineering software is free for students?


Tool Student access (checked 18 Nov 2026)


**AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D** Autodesk Education plan: free one-year access for qualifying students, renewable while you remain eligible. Learning use only.


**Tekla Structures** Tekla Student Subscription: free, valid 365 days from activation, educational use only, output is watermarked ([Tekla Campus](https://www.tekla.com/solutions/campus/student-subscription) ).


**STAAD.Pro and other Bentley tools** Bentley Education gives students free software for educational, non-commercial use. Check your entitlement after signing up.


**ETABS, SAP2000** No free student licence found on CSI's site. Most students use them in the college lab.


**QGIS** Free and open source (GPL), "free of charge if downloaded from QGIS.org".


The useful consequence: you can install AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D, Tekla and QGIS on your own laptop for free. That only works if the laptop runs Windows and meets the Revit floor.

## Recommended laptop specs for civil engineering students


We deliberately do not quote rupee prices. Configurations, GST and festival sales move them every few weeks, and no official source gives a stable figure. Buy against these specs instead.


### Tier 1: 1st and 2nd year (AutoCAD, STAAD.Pro, QGIS, small Revit models)


- **CPU:** a current 6- to 8-core Intel Core i5/Core Ultra 5 or AMD Ryzen 5/7 (H-series if possible).
- **RAM:** **16 GB** , upgradable.
- **GPU:** discrete NVIDIA GeForce RTX with at least **4 GB** (Revit's minimum).
- **Storage:** **512 GB NVMe SSD.** AutoCAD and Civil 3D suggest an SSD; Revit alone needs 30 GB plus temp space.
- **OS:** Windows 11.


### Tier 2: 3rd and 4th year (Revit BIM projects, ETABS, SAP2000, Tekla)


- **CPU:** Intel Core i7/Core Ultra 7 or AMD Ryzen 7, H-series.
- **RAM:** **32 GB** (Revit's "value" tier, AutoCAD's and Civil 3D's recommendation).
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060-class with **8 GB** (Revit "performance", AutoCAD recommended, Tekla tier 1).
- **Storage:** **1 TB NVMe SSD.** CSI recommends a 500 GB or larger PCIe SSD for ETABS.


### Tier 3: thesis and large building models


- **RAM:** **64 GB** (CSI's recommendation for ETABS and SAP2000; Revit "performance").
- **GPU:** 8 GB or more of video memory.
- Consider a desktop if you work at a fixed desk. It gives more performance per rupee and runs cooler than any laptop.


## What to check before you pay


- **Your syllabus.** If your college teaches ETABS and Revit, plan for Tier 2 by third year.
- **Upgradable RAM.** Search the exact model number with "RAM slots". Soldered 16 GB cannot grow.
- **A real NVIDIA GPU.** "Graphics: shared" on a spec sheet means integrated graphics.
- **Windows 11.** Tekla Structures 2026 supports Windows 11 only.
- **Two-monitor output.** Trimble recommends two-monitor support for Tekla; a second screen also helps for drawings and models side by side.
